comment.narrative: Two institutions were selected as winners of the BIC Ethiopia AgriFinance Lab an outofthebox financing innovation competition. Commercial Bank of Ethiopia Developed a solution called Movable collateral asset finance and insurance. Within this innovative solution the bank seeks to introduce movable collateral asset registry technology by deploying a mobile platformapplication and the required tools to identify and register the movable collateral e.g. livestock in an efficient and reliable manner. Kacha developed a solution called Agri MSME Finance. The aim is to provide access to suitable financial products for agriMSMEs empowering them to thrive. With this aim Kacha seeks to streamline the loan processes improving risk assessment and expediting loan approvals by means of data analytics and automation.

The study summarises the mapping policy landscape financing challenges recommendations and provides an overview of current financing instruments accessible for agricultural SMEs in Ethiopia but also from other countries as an inspiration for the Ethiopian ecosystem. It is available at the download section of the BIC Ethiopia website.

title.narrative: BIC Incubatees and incubators performance monitoring system

description.narrative: BIC Incubatees and incubators performance monitoring system

comment.narrative: Given the ambitious indicators and the number of players it was planned to develop an efficient incubators performance monitoring system. The team checked several options available in the market as well as the tracking cockpit ice180.com a software developed by IceAddis one of the pioneer incubators in Ethiopia. Parallel a monitoring needs assessment for BIC Ethiopia was conducted and the monitoring requirements of the project were compared with the options available. It became clear that none of the offers matched the requirements and that a tailormade solution was necessary. The most efficient way to realise the needed monitoring system was identified and this was a solution based on the structure of ice180.com. Currently the project works together with a software developer on an advanced and modified version of ice180.com that will address all specific monitoring requirements of BIC Ethiopia. Several beta versions were tested by the team and the final version is expected to be realized in 2023. Since the development of the electronic monitoring system takes longer than expected and was not finished when the implementation of the starter and catalyser trainings started the team works with an interim solution based on Excel.

comment.narrative: Based on inputs of the first practitioners dialogue the participants created BIC ETH INCUBATORS a social media expert group as active communication channel among incubators startups and MSMEs. It was considered the fasted and most practical approach to establish a regular exchange platform for close collaboration between the incubators and their potential clients and serves as a simple form of learning platform. During the interviews done by the ROM consultant the practicality of the approach was confirmed by the incubators and that the social media expert group is still active.

Benchmarking study on incubators in regional ecosystems in Africa.

comment.narrative: The mapping of Entrepreneur Support Organisations ESOs is finalized and the data analysis was performed. Summary of the results were presented during the BIC Ethiopia Opening Conference in October 2022. In January 2023 a representative group of 16 ESOs and industry stakeholders were convened for a workshop to provide their input and feedback on the mapping output and address areas that would need review. The forming Ethiopian Association of Startup Ecosystem EASE were furthermore involved in the validation. Data is the basis for the benchmarking with the regional ecosystem. As the project has only surveyed and mapped Ethiopia the benchmarking relies on the availability on relatively comparable data sets. The relevant and benchmarkable regional ecosystems were identified Kenya Uganda and possibly Rwanda. The potential data sources were also approached ASSEK in Kenya ANDE and StartupBlink for Uganda. The actual benchmarking and the formulation of the study including the presentation of the results will take place later in 2023.

description.narrative: Guidebook Capacity Building for Incubation Hubs

comment.narrative: A BIC Incubator Toolkit has been developed by BIC Ethiopia to support you as Ethiopian incubators to address the challenges listed below in the context of the BIC Ethiopia project that were identified by the Ethiopian incubator ecosystemLack of a supportive environment Lack of experts to enable start ups to take ideas into viable business models Annual intake is limited and fragmented Number of in house experts is very limited plus it is difficult to retain experts due to a lack of funding High costs of running hubs Lack of capacity building for incubation managersThe toolkit contains a set of 17 design thinking tools addressing the aforementioned bottlenecks and guides the incubator to Clearly define and understand its portfolio and business model Refine its strategy and develop a growth strategy Manage its finances identify funding needs and opportunities to boost its organisational impact Develop human capacities to sustain its team and organisation Refine marketing strategy and get digital to scale its business

Eleven incubators were selected and joined BIC Ethiopia. Together with the four preidentified incubators of the consortium partners the number of fifteen 15 incubators was reached. All incubators received first capacity building trainingsJune 20 23 ToT for 7 incubatorsOctober 17 20 ToT for 7 incubatorsOctober 2425 ToT for 1 incubator newly established incubator of MfM in Agro Technical and Technology College in Harar.The first practitioner dialogue was facilitated in October 14 and attended by all incubators.Organisational sustainability workshops for individual incubators were conducted for the three newly established incubators Ice Hawassa Addis Ababa Chamber of Commerce and ATTC in Harar. In 2023 the other incubators will have their individual organisational sustainability workshops and all will receive further ToT trainings.

Outside Addis Ababa incubation services to MSMEs are rarely available while youth unemployment is particularly high. BIC aims to decentralize the availability of incubation services in the Southern Ethiopian region and the Northern regions by facilitating the establishment of new incubators.

comment.narrative: The incubator Icehawassa in Hawassa is the first one that is operational and will be officially launched in November. The other two incubators are from the Addis Chamber of Commerce and Sectoral Association AACCSA and from Menschen fr Menschen MfM are in the process of establishing their incubator and getting operational. Both were able to recruit an incubation manager and secured a space for setting up the incubator. BIC Ethiopias team continuously supports them continuously in the process.
